[00:00] Jordan: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll run through a quick agenda, mostly intake and making sure we don't miss any regulatory bits — hi Alyssa, hi Marco.
[00:12] Alyssa: hi yeah thanks, I uh appreciate you fitting us in. We're just heads down for an upcoming internal audit and want to line up what we need from Redwood.
[00:19] Priya: great, can you outline the primary concerns, Alyssa? like data residency or access to the reports?
[00:25] Alyssa: both. data residency for PHI-ish data flows, also evidence that's shareable with our auditors and a control mapping that shows who in our org will attest to each control.
[00:35] Marco: and on the infra side we need to see KMS handshake patterns, specifically whether you support customer-managed keys in a VPC/private deployment.
[00:43] Ethan: quick note, we support both cloud KMS integrations and bring-your-own-HSM in Private mode; there are a couple of integration patterns — we usually provide a flow diagram and a short script to verify encrypt/decrypt.
[00:54] Hannah: when you say "flow diagram" is that in the Trust Center or a separate doc? we need something we can give to our security team.
[00:59] Jordan: both — we can put a high level diagram in the Trust Center and attach a more detailed integration playbook. we'll share a redacted example of our SOC 2 Type II report as well.
[01:06] Kenji: auditor question: do you surface token-level request logs with timestamps and request IDs that we can reconcile? like for an access control test.
[01:14] Priya: yes, we emit request/response traces with request IDs, model version, timestamp, and route; retention is configurable — default 90 days for hosted, can be longer for Dedicated/Private. For Private, you can push logs to your S3 or SIEM.
[01:29] Kenji: okay that's promising, retention policy and chain-of-custody is important to us.
[01:33] Marco: also want to understand RBAC, specifically delegation for engineers vs compliance. We don't want our SREs to have keys to production models.
[01:42] Jordan: our RBAC supports scoped roles and can integrate with your SSO via SAML/SCIM; we have a delegated admin role and can limit access to model pinning and rollout controls.
[01:50] Alyssa: can you share an example role matrix?
[01:53] Priya: yes, we'll attach a role matrix. it shows least privilege roles and example permissions.
[01:58] Hannah: on encryption — we need to confirm that customer-managed keys mean we control key rotation and KMS policies; if Redwood can see plaintext in certain modes that's a blocker.
[02:08] Ethan: good question, so in Private mode with CMK, Redwood does not have key material; the service performs envelope encryption where the customer KMS unwraps only within your environment. In Hosted there's an option but by default keys are host-managed.
[02:21] Alyssa: so for our audit we'll need a statement saying Redwood doesn't have access to plaintext under the Private+CMK config.
[02:28] Jordan: we'll provide an attestation snippet and a diagram. we'll also include sample KMS policies customers use.
[02:34] Kenji: about the controls mapping — we need a CSV that maps each SOC 2/ISO control to Redwood artifacts or procedures and a named owner on our side.
[02:42] Priya: we have a controls mapping template; we'll pre-populate Redwood columns (where we map to policies, screenshots, and Trust Center reports) and leave customer columns blank for you to fill.
[02:52] Alyssa: that would be helpful. also can you confirm retention windows for audit logs across environments? we heard "configurable" but need concrete numbers for the audit plan.
[03:02] Priya: sure — hosted default 90 days, Dedicated can be configured to 365+ with an SLA, Private depends on your storage — we recommend at least 1 year for production audit windows; we can show cost tradeoffs.
[03:15] Marco: about PoC — we want a small pilot to exercise KMS, log export to Splunk, and a quantized model path to look at latency. how long does that usually take?
[03:26] Ethan: typical PoC is 2-3 weeks: week one infra setup (VPC peering, KMS creds, Trust Center access), week two run traffic and collect traces, week three analyze and handoff artifacts. we can compress to 10 working days if needed.
[03:39] Alyssa: timeline — our audit window planning shows February 2027 for readiness. we need to finalize scope by mid-November.
[03:46] Jordan: ok so action: Jordan will share SOC 2 redacted pages + Trust Center link by 2026-11-02, Priya will schedule PoC kickoff and share the controls template, Alyssa will send in-scope system list.
[03:57] Marco: another question — do you provide exportable control evidence packages (zip of screenshots + logs) for auditors?
[04:03] Priya: yes, we can create export bundles, with role-based filters, and a signed manifest. for some items we provide attestation docs rather than raw evidence.
[04:13] Kenji: any third-party penetration test reports?
[04:16] Jordan: we have a pen-test summary we can share under an NDA; for full reports we usually require a data sharing agreement.
[04:23] Alyssa: ok we'll flag that if auditors request it.
[04:27] Hannah: small nit — in the Trust Center, is there a way to restrict certain team members to "read-only auditor" roles? we don't want internal engineers poking at evidence.
[04:36] Priya: yes you can create auditor tokens with scoped read-only access and expiration.
[04:41] Jordan: cool, i'll include that in the next email.
[04:44] Alyssa: great, thanks everyone. any other blockers?
[04:47] Marco: none from infra.
[04:49] Kenji: none.
[04:50] Jordan: wrap up then — recap of next steps, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the PoC and share the docs. thanks all.

End of call.
